raw_text: The Indian Chronicles case presents a unique contribution to the academic study of information operations. Unlike well-documented Russian and Chinese IO campaigns that primarily operate through social media manipulation, the Indian Chronicles network employed a legacy media impersonation strategy at unprecedented scale. Our comparative analysis positions this operation along three novel dimensions: (1) temporal persistence — 15 years of continuous operation makes it the longest-documented IO campaign, (2) institutional penetration — achieving UN ECOSOC consultative status for shell NGOs represents a qualitative escalation beyond social media influence, and (3) geographic distribution — 116 countries far exceeds the reach of previously documented operations. We propose the term 'institutional influence operation' to distinguish this category from social media-centric IO campaigns.
